findings.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls a no-argument method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist in UsernameForm or any of its ancestors. The new guard `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` references a symbol only defined in UsernamePasswordForm (protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), backed by the webauthnAuth field, which UsernameForm does not have); the PR does not compile — every build of services fails with a cannot-find-symbol error, so nothing in this diff can ever run.

[BUG] The moved webauthn setup is now gated on user != null, so fillContextForm is never invoked on the initial login page when no user is identified, removing the conditional-UI (username autocomplete) setup the old code performed. On the first visit to the username/password page (context.getUser() == null), WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm no longer runs, so the ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute / webauthn form is not rendered; the new test webauthnLoginWithExternalKey in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest asserts `getUsernameAutocomplete()` is 'username webauthn' and the //form[@id='webauth'] exists right after oauth.openLoginForm() with no user selected, so that assertion fails against this code.

[BUG] challenge(context, error, field) drops the fillContextForm call for the unidentified-user case entirely, so the error/first-challenge page of a conditional-passkeys realm never carries webauthn data. Realms using the conditional passkeys flow that previously rendered the passkey option on the initial or error username/password challenge (user not yet identified) lose it; combined with the same user!=null guard in authenticate(), there is no code path left that calls fillContextForm with user==null, contradicting the retained comment 'setup webauthn data when possible'.

[ADVISORY] The new gating branch in UsernameForm.authenticate (`!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`) that conditionally re-enables the re-auth skip path is exercised by no test in this diff. Every new test added (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, PasskeysUsernameFormTest, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) runs against realms whose browser flow is switched to UsernamePasswordFormFactory (or other flows), so the UsernameForm behavior change is completely unverified; a regression in the skip logic (e.g. forcing re-auth users with linked brokers, or users with no passkey, back to a username form) ships unnoticed and bites any deployment using the default UsernameForm flow with the passkeys feature enabled.

[ADVISORY] The extracted setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError logic (setting LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED on re-auth error forms) is never verified by any test in the diff. The tests that hit the bad-password-during-re-auth path (webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey) assert only the error message and the presence of the webauthn form; if the refactor drops the auth-note check or the form attributes (e.g. wrong auth-note key, or the attributes not being read by the template), re-auth error pages would render a visible username field and a registration link — a phishing/identity-confusion surface for re-authenticating users — and no test would catch it.

[ADVISORY] The reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test wraps the webauthn-form absence assertion in `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception e) {}`, which swallows every exception type as 'expected'. Because findElement never returns null, the assertThat(nullValue()) line can only ever trigger fail(); the catch (Exception) also swallows genuine infrastructure failures such as page-load timeouts, driver errors, or an assertion error from a different matcher — so a broken login page in this scenario silently passes the test instead of failing it, hiding real regressions behind a verification that cannot fail for the right reason.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm's new guard calls a no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() while UsernamePasswordForm defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) with an additional user!=null check, and the diff shows no definition of the no-arg variant in UsernameForm. If the no-arg method exists with different gating semantics than the one-arg version (e.g. realm-policy-only without the user check), the two call sites on the same re-auth path diverge: UsernameForm disables the skip purely on realm passkeys policy for users who may have no passkey at all, forcing such users to a re-enter-username step during prompt=login — an edge case (realm passkeys enabled, user has no passkey credential) that no test in the diff covers in a UsernameForm flow.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only version introduced in this diff is the one-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) defined in UsernamePasswordForm, and UsernameForm is a sibling class (both extend AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator), so no inherited or local no-arg method exists in the diff. The branch as shown does not compile; if a no-arg helper exists outside the diff, its logic (which realm policy / which user it consults) is untraceable to any requirement in this change.

[BUG] The webauthn form setup in authenticate() was moved from a user-independent gate ("if (webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())") to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null, so the anonymous first-visit username/password page no longer initializes conditional passkey UI. A first-time (non re-auth) visitor to a UsernamePasswordForm-only flow with passkeys enabled gets no conditional-UI/autocomplete setup — a regression of normal login behavior that goes beyond the stated re-authentication fix and is not traceable to any requirement in the intent.

[ADVISORY] The diff flips passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey from asserting the webauthn form is absent after username selection to asserting it is present, silently changing normal-login conditional-UI behavior for users with non-discoverable keys rather than covering it with a new test. Realm admins running the browser flow for users whose passkeys are non-discoverable now see a WebAuthn button on the password step during ordinary (non re-auth) login; the behavior change rides along in a test assertion flip with no requirement or release-note traceability.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returns false unconditionally in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator, so during a re-authentication error the authenticator-list branch of fillContextForm is never taken even when the re-authenticating user has discoverable passkeys. The stated intent is 'passkeys should be possible during re-authentication', but on a failed passkey or password during re-auth the error page renders the conditional-UI path only (never the identified-user authenticator list); users whose browsers don't support conditional mediation lose the passkey option exactly in the scenario the PR claims to fix.

[ADVISORY] In webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey the shared setup's events.clear() after logout() was deleted as a side effect of splitting the original test, so the pre-re-auth events (initial passkey login event) are still queued when the first re-auth assertions begin. Future maintainers running or debugging this test see a stale login event interleaved with re-auth assertions, and the drift from the original test's event hygiene was not a deliberate part of the re-auth work — it is untraceable test churn.

[BUG] The refactor of fillContextForm gating in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate inverts the original condition: the old code explicitly set up WebAuthn conditional-UI data 'when the user is not already selected' (context.getUser() == null), while the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null, so the fresh-login page rendered by UsernamePasswordForm with passkeys enabled no longer receives the conditional-UI form attributes. On a fresh login (no user in authContext) through a browser flow using UsernamePasswordForm with the passkeys feature/policy enabled, fillContextForm is skipped, the login page loses the WebAuthn autocomplete/conditional-mediation setup, and browser passkey autofill silently disappears for first-time logins — the exact capability the removed 'user is not already selected' branch existed to provide; the diff's own passwordLoginWithExternalKey test asserts the webauthn form is present on a fresh openLoginForm(), which this code path no longer produces.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate's skip condition changed from 'user already set and no linked brokers → success' to also require !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(), so when passkeys are enabled and a re-authenticating user HAS a linked identity provider, the username form is no longer skipped and the user is dumped onto the username/password+conditional-UI page instead of being routed to their broker. Users who linked an external IdP and previously re-authenticated via that IdP (the hasLinkedBrokers path this very branch was guarding) are now shown the username form on every re-authentication once the realm enables passkeys, breaking the existing IdP re-authentication behavior the adjacent hasLinkedBrokers check exists to preserve.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators returns false unconditionally even when context.getUser() != null, so during conditional-UI re-authentication fillContextForm always takes the 'unidentified user' branch and renders a username-entry conditional-UI form for a user the server has already identified. Re-authenticating users with conditional passkeys are shown a username field backed by conditional UI even though their identity is known; the page relies on USERNAME_HIDDEN being set only when an error occurs (via setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError), so the success-path re-auth form displays an editable/visible username input that the browser autofill flow, not the server, is trusted to resolve — a UX/integrity divergence between the error path and the happy path that the next template change can break.

[ADVISORY] The reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test asserts element absence by wrapping an assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()) in try/catch(Exception) with a fail(), a construct that 'passes' through the catch whenever findElement throws and can never meaningfully assert the nullValue matcher. Because findElement throws NoSuchElementException when the element is absent (the expected case), the nullValue assertion line is dead code reached only when the element exists — and then the resulting AssertionError is an Error, not an Exception, so it escapes the catch and fails correctly only by accident; the next editor who widens the catch to Throwable or copies this pattern into a test where the element can be either present or absent will get a test that goes green while the page state is wrong.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added in this diff is the protected isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) on UsernamePasswordForm, which UsernameForm does not extend, so this is either a compile error against the shown diff or relies on an undefined method. The branch does not compile (no no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled exists on UsernameForm's hierarchy in this diff), or, if such a method exists elsewhere with different semantics, the passkeys-skip decision in UsernameForm diverges from the user-aware check in UsernamePasswordForm, and re-authenticating users without passkey credentials are forced through a username form they previously skipped.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled checks only webauthnAuth presence, realm passkeys-enabled flag, and user != null — it never checks whether the user actually possesses a WebAuthn credential, so the passkey UI is rendered for re-authenticating users with zero passkeys. A realm admin enables passkeys, a password-only user triggers re-auth (prompt=login), and the login page shows a webauthn/passkey control that fails with an error when clicked; the new test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only covers the passkeysEnabled=FALSE case and explicitly leaves this passkeys-enabled-but-no-credential case untested.

[ADVISORY] The diff inverts a previously-asserted behavior without any stated acceptance: the old test explicitly asserted the webauthn form is NOT present on the username/password page after the user was identified with a non-discoverable key, and this diff rewrites both the assertion and the comment ('Passkeys still enabled') to match the new implementation instead of the old constraint. The prior test encoded an accepted product constraint (no passkey UI once user is known to have only a non-discoverable key); flipping it to match the code is intent drift — if the constraint was real, organizations flows now surface a passkey option that cannot succeed for that user.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is overridden to return false unconditionally, which suppresses the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean list not only during the username/password step (the stated intent) but also whenever the conditional-UI authenticator renders a challenge for an already-identified user, changing base-class 2FA behavior for that flow. Users in the conditional-UI flow who were previously shown a picker of their registered passkey authenticators (identified-user path in WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm) now never see the list and are routed to the fallback path instead; the diff's own comment scopes the override to 'login with conditional passkeys' but the override has no condition, so it silently removes the identified-user list rendering everywhere this subclass runs.

[ADVISORY] The authenticate() change replaces the original 'fill webauthn data when the user is not already selected' call with a user!=null guard, so on a first-time (no user in context) login the authenticate path no longer calls fillContextForm at all — the conditional-UI setup for the initial login page now depends entirely on some other code path (e.g. the conditional-UI authenticator execution) that this diff does not show being preserved. If any deployment's flow relies on UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate to bootstrap conditional passkey mediation before the user is identified (the case the original comment explicitly handled), that page loses its passkey autofill and users must type a username; the tests only exercise the external-key flow where a separate WebAuthn conditional-UI execution renders the form.

[BUG] The refactor gates WebAuthn form setup on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null, so fillContextForm is no longer invoked on the initial username/password login page when no user has been identified (the regular, non-re-authentication login path). For a fresh login (user == null) with the passkeys feature enabled, the conditional-mediation WebAuthn data (script/attributes that let the browser offer passkey autofill on the login page) is never populated, so users who rely on discoverable passkey autofill on the username/password page can no longer sign in that way — the previous code explicitly ran fillContextForm when the user was not selected. The author's counter-argument is that conditional UI is now handled elsewhere (UsernameForm) or by the template; that fails because UsernamePasswordForm-based flows (the exact flow these tests configure via switchExecutionInBrowserFormToProvider) render the username/password page through authenticate() and no longer receive the webauthn attributes, breaking passkey-first login for realms using this flow.

[ADVISORY] When passkeys are enabled, the username form is now rendered during re-authentication (context.getUser() != null) with an editable username field, while USERNAME_HIDDEN is only set on the error path (AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError) and not on the initial re-auth challenge. Operators and users on realms with conditional passkeys see the username field during prompt=login re-authentication even when the session user is already fixed; a user who types a different username during a re-auth gets an 'invalid password' against the session user (the USER_SET_BEFORE path validates credentials against context.getUser()), producing confusing errors and a behavior divergence between the first render and the post-error render of the same page — worth either hiding the username on the initial re-auth challenge too or documenting why it must be shown.

[ADVISORY] The webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication test cannot distinguish a genuine passkey re-authentication from silent reuse of the existing SSO session, so it passes even if the re-auth fix regresses. After prompt=login the test only asserts appPage.assertCurrent() and a matching LOGIN event; if Keycloak ignores prompt=login for passkey users and reuses the cached session (the exact bug class this PR fixes), the same assertions still hold and the regression ships undetected. Same pattern in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication (lines 309-321).

[ADVISORY] The reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test uses try/catch around an assertion with a bare catch (Exception nsee), so any driver failure other than element-absence (timeout, stale element, WebDriver error) is swallowed and treated as the expected outcome. The try block asserts assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()) then fail(); an AssertionError correctly propagates, but any RuntimeException from the driver is silently accepted as 'webauthn button absent', giving a false pass on a broken page — inconsistent with the Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) pattern used in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest for the same check.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff asserts the actual effect of the new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError — that USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED are set on the form after a failed re-auth password attempt. Checked PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, PasskeysUsernameFormTest, and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest: after the 'Invalid password.' step in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey (~line 371), the tests assert only the webauthn form presence and error text, never that the username field is hidden — a regression that re-renders the re-auth form with a visible username input (masking which user is re-authenticating) passes all tests in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The new error-path call AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) inside createErrorResponse is exercised by no test that fails a passkey during re-authentication in this diff. All new tests use a passing virtual authenticator; the conditional-UI error challenge during re-authentication (wrong PIN / user verification failure on the prompt=login flow) is an untriggered new branch — a broken error page after a failed passkey re-auth attempt ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] In webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, the incorrect-password step asserts the error text but no events.expect(EventType.LOGIN_ERROR).error(Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS) assertion is made, so a regression in the badPasswordHandler event emission (e.g. dropping the INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS error event, which auditors rely on) is invisible to this diff's tests. Brute-force protection/audit consumers get silently wrong events for failed re-auth attempts; the earlier passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey test asserts the error event for the non-reauth path, showing the authors know the pattern but omitted it for the new re-auth-with-user-set path (where the diff moved code out of badPasswordHandler).

[BUG] challenge(context, error, field) now gates webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) behind isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null, so the passkey conditional-UI data is no longer set up when the challenge is re-rendered for an unidentified user. In a passkeys-enabled realm using the combined UsernamePasswordForm, when a user fails the first step (wrong password, wrong username, or empty submission — cases where context.getUser() is still null), the re-rendered error page comes back without the webauthn form/conditional-UI attributes: previously the old code explicitly called fillContextForm when 'the user is not already selected', so a passwordless user could still invoke passkey autofill after a typo; now the passkey option silently disappears from the error page and the user must reload the login form to use their passkey. Earlier flow executions (the conditional-UI authenticator) do not re-run on an action() request, so nothing else re-establishes this data.

[BUG] authenticate() moved the fillContextForm call out from the formData block but kept it gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) with user != null, so the initial (user-not-yet-identified) username/password page in a passkeys realm no longer gets webauthn data from this authenticator. Any flow where UsernamePasswordForm is the execution responsible for setting up conditional passkey mediation while the user is anonymous loses the webauthn form/conditional-UI attributes on its first render, breaking passkey autofill on the initial login page and on every re-challenge while the user remains unidentified; the new tests only assert webauthn presence after the user was identified (via UsernameForm) or during re-authentication, so this path is untested and the regression is invisible to the suite.

[ADVISORY] createErrorResponse now calls setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError and then fillContextForm — whose new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override unconditionally returns false — during passkey failure, and no test in the diff exercises this path under re-authentication (prompt=login). If the interplay of the forced-false shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators with the re-auth form attributes mis-renders (e.g., passkey UI dropped or username field re-exposed after a failed passkey attempt during re-auth), operators debugging conditional-passkey re-auth failures get no signal from the test suite; a regression here would surface only as a broken re-auth error page in production.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, both the initial `authenticate()` path and the error `challenge(context, error, field)` path used to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` specifically when `context.getUser() == null` and passkeys were enabled. This diff replaces those conditions with `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. As a result, there is no longer any code path in this class that calls `fillContextForm` for the unidentified-user (user==null) case, even though the comment still implies setup is done when possible. This matches the finding’s claim about losing webauthn/passkeys form setup on the first/error username/password challenge when the user is not yet identified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a behavior change in `UsernameForm.authenticate` by tightening the re-authentication fast-path from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, which is nontrivial gating logic. In this diff, the added/modified tests shown are primarily in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` (explicitly switching the browser flow to `UsernamePasswordFormFactory`) and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`; none of the test changes shown clearly configure or assert behavior of the default `UsernameForm` re-auth skip path (e.g., whether the username form is skipped/shown under conditional passkeys, linked brokers, or users without passkeys). This is a specific, diff-grounded “missing test coverage for new branch” concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new helper `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` that sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` based on the auth-note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` (now made `public` for the static import). This helper is now called from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler(...)` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`. The newly added/updated tests exercise re-authentication flows and bad-password cases (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`), but they only assert messages like "Invalid password." and the presence/absence of the `//form[@id='webauth']` element; they do not assert UI state tied to `USERNAME_HIDDEN` / `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` (e.g., that the username field is hidden or registration link is disabled) nor that the correct auth-note key is honored. So a regression in the extracted logic (wrong note key, attributes not set) would not be caught by the tests in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()`, the diff adds two blocks that check absence of `//form[@id='webauth']` by wrapping `driver.findElement(...)` in `try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. This will treat *any* `Exception` (e.g., generic `WebDriverException`, timeouts, session/driver failures) as “expected”, allowing the test to pass for the wrong reason and potentially masking real regressions/infrastructure failures. The intent is specifically to accept `NoSuchElementException`, but the code swallows all exceptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm's new guard calls a no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() while UsernamePasswordForm defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) with an additional user!=null check, and the diff shows no definition of the no-arg variant in UsernameForm. If the no-arg method exists with different gating semantics than the one-arg version (e.g. realm-policy-only without the user check), the two call sites on the same re-auth path diverge: UsernameForm disables the skip purely on realm passkeys policy for users who may have no passkey at all, forcing such users to a re-enter-username step during prompt=login — an edge case (realm passkeys enabled, user has no passkey credential) that no test in the diff covers in a UsernameForm flow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now gates the re-auth skip with `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg) while `UsernamePasswordForm` introduces `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` requiring `user != null`. The diff does not show what `UsernameForm`’s no-arg method does (it may exist outside the shown hunk or be inherited), so the exact semantics can’t be verified here; however, the finding is grounded in a real potential inconsistency between two closely related code paths and highlights a specific uncovered edge case (realm passkeys enabled + re-authenticated user lacking passkey) not explicitly exercised by the added tests (the new ‘no passkey’ test is in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` with realm passkeys disabled, not the `UsernameForm` skip logic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only version introduced in this diff is the one-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) defined in UsernamePasswordForm, and UsernameForm is a sibling class (both extend AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator), so no inherited or local no-arg method exists in the diff. The branch as shown does not compile; if a no-arg helper exists outside the diff, its logic (which realm policy / which user it consults) is untraceable to any requirement in this change.
matched_golden_ids: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue highlights that UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments even though the available method signature is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), causing a compile/error and missing the required UserModel parameter. This is the same underlying problem as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn form setup in authenticate() was moved from a user-independent gate ("if (webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())") to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null, so the anonymous first-visit username/password page no longer initializes conditional passkey UI. A first-time (non re-auth) visitor to a UsernamePasswordForm-only flow with passkeys enabled gets no conditional-UI/autocomplete setup — a regression of normal login behavior that goes beyond the stated re-authentication fix and is not traceable to any requirement in the intent.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()`, the call to `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` was moved from the prior passkeys-enabled check to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which explicitly requires `user != null` (new method at end of class). This prevents `fillContextForm` from running when `context.getUser()` is null (typical initial/anonymous login page). Additionally, `challenge(context, String error, String field)` previously *only* filled webauthn context when `context.getUser() == null && passkeys enabled`, but now uses the same `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, flipping the condition and removing setup for the anonymous case. From the diff alone, this is a behavior regression for first-visit UsernamePasswordForm flows with passkeys enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff flips passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey from asserting the webauthn form is absent after username selection to asserting it is present, silently changing normal-login conditional-UI behavior for users with non-discoverable keys rather than covering it with a new test. Realm admins running the browser flow for users whose passkeys are non-discoverable now see a WebAuthn button on the password step during ordinary (non re-auth) login; the behavior change rides along in a test assertion flip with no requirement or release-note traceability.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior so that WebAuthn/passkeys UI is filled/shown when a user is already identified (i.e., after username selection): `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` and `challenge()` now call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper explicitly requires `user != null`. This is reinforced by the test change in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, which flips from asserting the `//form[@id='webauth']` is absent to asserting it is present on the username/password step. That is a user-visible UX/behavior change during ordinary login flows (not just re-authentication) and could merit explicit rationale/release-note/PR description, but it is not verifiably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returns false unconditionally in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator, so during a re-authentication error the authenticator-list branch of fillContextForm is never taken even when the re-authenticating user has discoverable passkeys. The stated intent is 'passkeys should be possible during re-authentication', but on a failed passkey or password during re-auth the error page renders the conditional-UI path only (never the identified-user authenticator list); users whose browsers don't support conditional mediation lose the passkey option exactly in the scenario the PR claims to fix.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly makes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` gate the “identified user / show authenticators list” logic behind `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` and then overrides that in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` to return `false` unconditionally. Therefore, when `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is invoked during re-authentication error handling (now more often, e.g. `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge()` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()`), the authenticator-list branch will indeed never run for the conditional-UI variant even if `context.getUser() != null`. However, the claim that this definitively removes the user’s passkey option for browsers without conditional mediation is not directly verifiable from the shown diff (it depends on template/UI behavior not included). This is still a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case/scope concern about missing fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey the shared setup's events.clear() after logout() was deleted as a side effect of splitting the original test, so the pre-re-auth events (initial passkey login event) are still queued when the first re-auth assertions begin. Future maintainers running or debugging this test see a stale login event interleaved with re-auth assertions, and the drift from the original test's event hygiene was not a deliberate part of the re-auth work — it is untraceable test churn.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove an `events.clear()` after `logout()` in the new `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` test, but the test does not perform any `events.expect...` assertions until after it calls `events.clear()` (right before the first re-auth passkey `events.expectLogin()` assertion). Therefore, any initial login event is explicitly cleared before the first re-auth event assertions, so there is no verifiable stale/queued event interleaving with re-auth assertions based on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The refactor of fillContextForm gating in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate inverts the original condition: the old code explicitly set up WebAuthn conditional-UI data 'when the user is not already selected' (context.getUser() == null), while the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null, so the fresh-login page rendered by UsernamePasswordForm with passkeys enabled no longer receives the conditional-UI form attributes. On a fresh login (no user in authContext) through a browser flow using UsernamePasswordForm with the passkeys feature/policy enabled, fillContextForm is skipped, the login page loses the WebAuthn autocomplete/conditional-mediation setup, and browser passkey autofill silently disappears for first-time logins — the exact capability the removed 'user is not already selected' branch existed to provide; the diff's own passwordLoginWithExternalKey test asserts the webauthn form is present on a fresh openLoginForm(), which this code path no longer produces.

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate and in its error challenge override, the diff changes when webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is invoked. Previously, the challenge path explicitly did it only when context.getUser() == null (fresh login / user not selected): `if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }`. Now it does it only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and that helper requires `user != null`. That means on a fresh login where no user is in the auth context, UsernamePasswordForm no longer calls fillContextForm at all, so the form attributes that enable conditional passkeys UI (set inside WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm) won’t be set by this authenticator. This is a behavior inversion visible in the diff and plausibly removes passkey conditional/autofill on first-time login pages using UsernamePasswordForm.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate's skip condition changed from 'user already set and no linked brokers → success' to also require !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(), so when passkeys are enabled and a re-authenticating user HAS a linked identity provider, the username form is no longer skipped and the user is dumped onto the username/password+conditional-UI page instead of being routed to their broker. Users who linked an external IdP and previously re-authenticated via that IdP (the hasLinkedBrokers path this very branch was guarding) are now shown the username form on every re-authentication once the realm enables passkeys, breaking the existing IdP re-authentication behavior the adjacent hasLinkedBrokers check exists to preserve.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate` from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`. This only affects whether the “reauthentication short-circuit” block runs when passkeys/conditional UI is enabled. Within that block, the `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` logic is unchanged: users *with* linked brokers were already not short-circuited (`context.success()` only happens when `!hasLinkedBrokers`). So the finding’s claim that linked-IdP reauthentication used to be skipped/routed differently and is now broken is not supported by the shown code change. The only clearly implied behavior change is for reauth users without linked brokers: they may no longer skip the username form when conditional passkeys are enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators returns false unconditionally even when context.getUser() != null, so during conditional-UI re-authentication fillContextForm always takes the 'unidentified user' branch and renders a username-entry conditional-UI form for a user the server has already identified. Re-authenticating users with conditional passkeys are shown a username field backed by conditional UI even though their identity is known; the page relies on USERNAME_HIDDEN being set only when an error occurs (via setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError), so the success-path re-auth form displays an editable/visible username input that the browser autofill flow, not the server, is trusted to resolve — a UX/integrity divergence between the error path and the happy path that the next template change can break.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` was changed to gate the “user identified” branch on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` rather than `context.getUser() != null`. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` then overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` to always return `false`, so `fillContextForm()` will never execute the branch that assumes an already-identified user (and will leave `isUserIdentified` false) even when `context.getUser()` is set. The finding’s downstream UI/template consequences (username field visibility, reliance on `USERNAME_HIDDEN` only on error paths) are not directly verifiable from the shown diff, but the control-flow coupling between “show authenticators” and “treat user as identified” is real and could be an architectural/edge-case concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test asserts element absence by wrapping an assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()) in try/catch(Exception) with a fail(), a construct that 'passes' through the catch whenever findElement throws and can never meaningfully assert the nullValue matcher. Because findElement throws NoSuchElementException when the element is absent (the expected case), the nullValue assertion line is dead code reached only when the element exists — and then the resulting AssertionError is an Error, not an Exception, so it escapes the catch and fails correctly only by accident; the next editor who widens the catch to Throwable or copies this pattern into a test where the element can be either present or absent will get a test that goes green while the page state is wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()`, the test checks absence of `//form[@id='webauth']` via `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception) {}`. In Selenium, `findElement` never returns null: it either returns a `WebElement` (non-null) or throws `NoSuchElementException` when absent. So the `nullValue()` assertion is effectively dead/meaningless for the “absent” case (it’s bypassed by the exception), and the test’s correctness relies on `AssertionError` (an `Error`, not `Exception`) escaping the catch when the element exists. This is a brittle anti-pattern but not a functional defect introduced by the diff, since the test will still fail when the element is present and pass when absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added in this diff is the protected isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) on UsernamePasswordForm, which UsernameForm does not extend, so this is either a compile error against the shown diff or relies on an undefined method. The branch does not compile (no no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled exists on UsernameForm's hierarchy in this diff), or, if such a method exists elsewhere with different semantics, the passkeys-skip decision in UsernameForm diverges from the user-aware check in UsernamePasswordForm, and re-authenticating users without passkey credentials are forced through a username form they previously skipped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (in `UsernameForm.java`), but the diff does not include the full `UsernameForm` class or its superclasses/interfaces, so it’s not verifiable from the diff alone that such a method does not already exist elsewhere in the hierarchy. The finding asserts a definite compile failure and specific semantic divergence, but the diff only proves a new call site, not the absence or semantics of the method definition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled checks only webauthnAuth presence, realm passkeys-enabled flag, and user != null — it never checks whether the user actually possesses a WebAuthn credential, so the passkey UI is rendered for re-authenticating users with zero passkeys. A realm admin enables passkeys, a password-only user triggers re-auth (prompt=login), and the login page shows a webauthn/passkey control that fails with an error when clicked; the new test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only covers the passkeysEnabled=FALSE case and explicitly leaves this passkeys-enabled-but-no-credential case untested.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true whenever `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, with no check that the identified user actually has any WebAuthn/passwordless credentials. The diff also changes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` to gate the “no authenticators” suppression behind `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that to `false`, meaning the usual `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()` path won’t run for conditional UI. Together, the diff plausibly causes the passkeys/webauthn UI to be populated for re-auth flows (`context.getUser()!=null`) even when the user has no passkeys, leading to a non-functional control. The added test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` only covers `passkeysEnabled=false` and does not exercise the `passkeysEnabled=true but user has no passkey` scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff inverts a previously-asserted behavior without any stated acceptance: the old test explicitly asserted the webauthn form is NOT present on the username/password page after the user was identified with a non-discoverable key, and this diff rewrites both the assertion and the comment ('Passkeys still enabled') to match the new implementation instead of the old constraint. The prior test encoded an accepted product constraint (no passkey UI once user is known to have only a non-discoverable key); flipping it to match the code is intent drift — if the constraint was real, organizations flows now surface a passkey option that cannot succeed for that user.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly notes a concrete behavioral inversion in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`: after `loginPage.loginUsername(USERNAME)`, the test comment and assertion change from expecting the WebAuthn form to be absent (`Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException...)`) to requiring it to be present (`driver.findElement(..."//form[@id='webauth']")`). This matches the implementation change where `UsernamePasswordForm` now calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (i.e., when a user is already set). However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this is a functional defect (it may be intended), so it’s best treated as an intent/behavior change that warrants explicit confirmation rather than a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is overridden to return false unconditionally, which suppresses the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean list not only during the username/password step (the stated intent) but also whenever the conditional-UI authenticator renders a challenge for an already-identified user, changing base-class 2FA behavior for that flow. Users in the conditional-UI flow who were previously shown a picker of their registered passkey authenticators (identified-user path in WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm) now never see the list and are routed to the fallback path instead; the diff's own comment scopes the override to 'login with conditional passkeys' but the override has no condition, so it silently removes the identified-user list rendering everywhere this subclass runs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm() depend on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) rather than just (user != null). In WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator this hook is overridden to always return false, so even when context.getUser() is already set, the code path that builds WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean (the identified-user authenticator list) will never run for this subclass. The finding’s broader claim about breaking 2FA behavior can’t be fully verified from the diff alone (we don’t see all call sites/flows), but the unconditional suppression and its potentially wider-than-comment scope is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The authenticate() change replaces the original 'fill webauthn data when the user is not already selected' call with a user!=null guard, so on a first-time (no user in context) login the authenticate path no longer calls fillContextForm at all — the conditional-UI setup for the initial login page now depends entirely on some other code path (e.g. the conditional-UI authenticator execution) that this diff does not show being preserved. If any deployment's flow relies on UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate to bootstrap conditional passkey mediation before the user is identified (the case the original comment explicitly handled), that page loses its passkey autofill and users must type a username; the tests only exercise the external-key flow where a separate WebAuthn conditional-UI execution renders the form.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a concrete behavior change in `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()`/`challenge()`: previously `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` was invoked when passkeys were enabled without requiring `context.getUser()` (the removed block explicitly said “when the user is not already selected”). After the change, both places call `fillContextForm` only via `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which returns true only if `user != null` (`protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) { return ... && user != null; }`). So, for flows where `UsernamePasswordForm` is the initial screen and no user is yet in the context, this authenticator no longer bootstraps WebAuthn/passkey UI data on that path, implicitly relying on some other execution (e.g., `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`) to set up the conditional UI. Whether that is a defect depends on the intended flow configuration (not shown in the diff), but the compatibility/coverage concern is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The refactor gates WebAuthn form setup on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null, so fillContextForm is no longer invoked on the initial username/password login page when no user has been identified (the regular, non-re-authentication login path). For a fresh login (user == null) with the passkeys feature enabled, the conditional-mediation WebAuthn data (script/attributes that let the browser offer passkey autofill on the login page) is never populated, so users who rely on discoverable passkey autofill on the username/password page can no longer sign in that way — the previous code explicitly ran fillContextForm when the user was not selected. The author's counter-argument is that conditional UI is now handled elsewhere (UsernameForm) or by the template; that fails because UsernamePasswordForm-based flows (the exact flow these tests configure via switchExecutionInBrowserFormToProvider) render the username/password page through authenticate() and no longer receive the webauthn attributes, breaking passkey-first login for realms using this flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the PR changes WebAuthn context setup from running when passkeys are enabled (previously unconditional in `authenticate()` and explicitly for `context.getUser() == null` in `challenge(error, field)`) to running only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper returns `... && user != null`. Concretely, both call sites now skip `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser()` is null (initial username/password page before any user is identified). The diff shows no alternative path in `UsernamePasswordForm` that populates those WebAuthn/passkeys form attributes for the fresh-login (user==null) render, so a regression for passkey-first/conditional UI on the initial login page is plausible and directly tied to this gating change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When passkeys are enabled, the username form is now rendered during re-authentication (context.getUser() != null) with an editable username field, while USERNAME_HIDDEN is only set on the error path (AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError) and not on the initial re-auth challenge. Operators and users on realms with conditional passkeys see the username field during prompt=login re-authentication even when the session user is already fixed; a user who types a different username during a re-auth gets an 'invalid password' against the session user (the USER_SET_BEFORE path validates credentials against context.getUser()), producing confusing errors and a behavior divergence between the first render and the post-error render of the same page — worth either hiding the username on the initial re-auth challenge too or documenting why it must be shown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` to no longer skip the username form during re-authentication when conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`). That makes the username screen appear even though a session user already exists. Separately, the only added/centralized logic to hide the username for re-authentication (`AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`, which sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED`) is invoked only on error paths (in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler()` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()`), and there is no corresponding call on the initial re-authentication challenge render. This creates a verifiable inconsistency introduced/exposed by the diff: initial re-auth screens can show an editable username, but after an error the same flow will hide it, leading to confusing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication test cannot distinguish a genuine passkey re-authentication from silent reuse of the existing SSO session, so it passes even if the re-auth fix regresses. After prompt=login the test only asserts appPage.assertCurrent() and a matching LOGIN event; if Keycloak ignores prompt=login for passkey users and reuses the cached session (the exact bug class this PR fixes), the same assertions still hold and the regression ships undetected. Same pattern in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication (lines 309-321).

adjudication.rationale: In both newly added tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` (in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`), the re-authentication step after `oauth.loginForm().prompt(OIDCLoginProtocol.PROMPT_VALUE_LOGIN).open()` only does `WaitUtils.waitForPageToLoad(); appPage.assertCurrent();` followed by `events.expectLogin()...`. Unlike other re-auth tests added in this diff (e.g., `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` asserts the re-auth UI message and presence/absence of the WebAuthn form), these discoverable-key tests do not assert that a re-authentication screen was actually shown or that an explicit re-auth flow occurred before landing on the app. This is a concrete test-gap tied to the new logic being validated (prompt=login re-auth behavior) rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test uses try/catch around an assertion with a bare catch (Exception nsee), so any driver failure other than element-absence (timeout, stale element, WebDriver error) is swallowed and treated as the expected outcome. The try block asserts assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()) then fail(); an AssertionError correctly propagates, but any RuntimeException from the driver is silently accepted as 'webauthn button absent', giving a false pass on a broken page — inconsistent with the Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) pattern used in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest for the same check.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff asserts the actual effect of the new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError — that USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED are set on the form after a failed re-auth password attempt. Checked PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, PasskeysUsernameFormTest, and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest: after the 'Invalid password.' step in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey (~line 371), the tests assert only the webauthn form presence and error text, never that the username field is hidden — a regression that re-renders the re-auth form with a visible username input (masking which user is re-authenticating) passes all tests in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new behavior centralized in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is true) and replaces the previous inline logic in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler()` with that call. The added/modified tests (notably `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`) assert the error text and presence of the webauthn form after an invalid password, but they do not assert the specific new/relocated effect on the rendered form (e.g., that the username is hidden / registration disabled during re-auth error). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly refactored logic, but not a verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new error-path call AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) inside createErrorResponse is exercised by no test that fails a passkey during re-authentication in this diff. All new tests use a passing virtual authenticator; the conditional-UI error challenge during re-authentication (wrong PIN / user verification failure on the prompt=login flow) is an untriggered new branch — a broken error page after a failed passkey re-auth attempt ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new error-path side effect in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator#createErrorResponse(...)` by calling `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` before `fillContextForm(context)`. The newly added/modified tests in `Passkeys*Test` classes exercise successful passkey logins during `prompt=login` re-authentication (and some password-failure paths), but none clearly trigger a *passkey failure* during re-authentication that would execute `createErrorResponse(...)` for conditional UI (e.g., failed user verification/PIN). Thus this is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly introduced logic, not a provable functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, the incorrect-password step asserts the error text but no events.expect(EventType.LOGIN_ERROR).error(Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS) assertion is made, so a regression in the badPasswordHandler event emission (e.g. dropping the INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS error event, which auditors rely on) is invisible to this diff's tests. Brute-force protection/audit consumers get silently wrong events for failed re-auth attempts; the earlier passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey test asserts the error event for the non-reauth path, showing the authors know the pattern but omitted it for the new re-auth-with-user-set path (where the diff moved code out of badPasswordHandler).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new re-authentication test coverage in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, including an intentional wrong-password attempt that only asserts UI text (`Assert.assertEquals("Invalid password.", loginPage.getInputError());`) but does not assert an emitted failure event (e.g., `events.expect(EventType.LOGIN_ERROR)...error(Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS)`). Since this PR refactors the re-authentication error-page setup by moving logic out of `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, the new re-auth path is a relevant place to assert audit/brute-force-relevant events. This is not a verifiable product bug from the diff (event emission `context.getEvent().error(Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS)` remains in `badPasswordHandler`), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for the newly emphasized re-authentication flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] challenge(context, error, field) now gates webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) behind isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null, so the passkey conditional-UI data is no longer set up when the challenge is re-rendered for an unidentified user. In a passkeys-enabled realm using the combined UsernamePasswordForm, when a user fails the first step (wrong password, wrong username, or empty submission — cases where context.getUser() is still null), the re-rendered error page comes back without the webauthn form/conditional-UI attributes: previously the old code explicitly called fillContextForm when 'the user is not already selected', so a passwordless user could still invoke passkey autofill after a typo; now the passkey option silently disappears from the error page and the user must reload the login form to use their passkey. Earlier flow executions (the conditional-UI authenticator) do not re-run on an action() request, so nothing else re-establishes this data.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the PR changes both the initial `authenticate()` path and the error re-render path `challenge(context, error, field)` to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true. But `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. This is a functional change from the previous code which called `fillContextForm` when passkeys were enabled even when no user was selected (old `challenge()` explicitly did this when `context.getUser() == null`). As a result, when the form is re-rendered for errors where `context.getUser()` remains null (e.g., unknown username / empty submission cases), the webauthn/passkey conditional-UI setup will not be re-applied, so the error page can lose the webauthn form/attributes compared to before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] authenticate() moved the fillContextForm call out from the formData block but kept it gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) with user != null, so the initial (user-not-yet-identified) username/password page in a passkeys realm no longer gets webauthn data from this authenticator. Any flow where UsernamePasswordForm is the execution responsible for setting up conditional passkey mediation while the user is anonymous loses the webauthn form/conditional-UI attributes on its first render, breaking passkey autofill on the initial login page and on every re-challenge while the user remains unidentified; the new tests only assert webauthn presence after the user was identified (via UsernameForm) or during re-authentication, so this path is untested and the regression is invisible to the suite.

[ADVISORY] createErrorResponse now calls setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError and then fillContextForm — whose new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override unconditionally returns false — during passkey failure, and no test in the diff exercises this path under re-authentication (prompt=login). If the interplay of the forced-false shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators with the re-auth form attributes mis-renders (e.g., passkey UI dropped or username field re-exposed after a failed passkey attempt during re-auth), operators debugging conditional-passkey re-auth failures get no signal from the test suite; a regression here would surface only as a broken re-auth error page in production.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);` into `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` before `fillContextForm(context)`. At the same time, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm(...)` was changed to only populate WebAuthn authenticators when `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` is true, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` now overrides that to always return `false` (comment: “Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys”). This means the conditional-passkey error path now explicitly combines “re-auth” form attributes (username hidden/registration disabled) with a fillContextForm that will not include the authenticator list/UI details. The added tests exercise successful passkey re-authentication via `prompt=login`, but none in the diff exercise a *failed* passkey attempt during re-auth (i.e., this `createErrorResponse` path under `prompt=login`), so regressions in the error page rendering/attributes would not be caught. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-coverage concern rather than a verifiable defect.
